original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: For six sources, exhaust all canonical thirteen-singleton words plus one final atomic TRIO whose total source-map counts are even and at least two; determine maximum paired-readout coverage among both possible 16-map profiles and price the best completion.
scope_change_reason: The initial simple-path-only search was widened once to include repeated prefix states and both possible restored 16-map multiplicity profiles. This makes the finite census complete for the selected one-TRIO, fourteen-source-call objective rather than excluding paths by a simplicity assumption.
bottleneck_link: The proposed operation could reduce recursive source-call/frame overhead while preserving the incumbent source-map application profile. The exact six-source census finds a two-readout deficit, so standard four-readout repairs make the completed unit-price bill worse than the incumbent.
stop_rule: Exhaust every length-13 restricted-growth word using all six labels whose sorted singleton counts are (1,2,2,2,3,3) or (1,1,2,2,2,5); allow repeated prefixes; stop after all leaves and direct-difference cross-check complete.
evidence: The full domain has 9,321,312 complete six-label RGS words, of which 2,342,340 match the two restored 16-map profiles. Incremental Python coverage and an independent direct-pair-difference C++ implementation agree on the complete histogram. Maximum paired coverage is 61/63 (88 words); no candidate covers 62 or 63. The exhibited maximum path repairs masks 11 and 40 with four readouts each, yielding 144 root calls versus the incumbent 142 at unit prices. No new kappa is claimed.
author: OpenAI Codex
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance in choosing the bounded construction hypothesis, writing and independently cross-checking the exact census implementations, deriving the completed cost equation, and preparing the report. No predecessor implementation was copied.

open_questions.question: Can two or more atomic TRIO calls reduce the completed six-source bill?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The one-TRIO path is exactly priced and does not improve at unit call costs; a second TRIO changes both the call-count frontier and the attainable prefix-difference set.
open_questions.first_step: Before enumerating, derive the optimistic fully charged source-map profiles for 12 singleton calls plus two TRIO calls and identify whether at least 63 masks can be paired with fewer than 126 output readouts.
open_questions.blocked_by: No blocker; it is a distinct future construction task and was outside this cycle's one bounded experiment.
